title: Context Fragment Resilience — scratch
body:
Purpose:
Quick personal log to characterize how partial context (fragmented KV-cache) impacts tail-latency and throughput under mixed-priority ingress. Trying to capture fast iterations and plausible actionable hypotheses rather than polished analysis.

Background / motivation:
- Observed odd p99 spikes when client requests contain very long histories but the cache service only has a partial KV for recent tokens. Suspect extra KV fetches + kernel path switch cause jitter.
- Want to quantify: how much latency penalty does a fragmented cache (partial prefill) impose across p50/p95/p99 and how that scales with qps and batching.

Environment / harness:
- Cluster: dev-dedicated-pool-3 (A100s), 8 GPUs, rw-runtime-2.1.1
- Model: rw-model-v2-13b (q4_k_mixed) with KV cache enabled
- Runtime flags: continuous-batching=true, early-kv-prefetch=true (toggle), splice-threshold-ms=8
- Load generator: local harness with poisson arrivals (lambda set per run), ability to attach long-context vs short-context payloads at tunable ratios
- Instrumentation: per-request trace-id, per-token timing, end-to-end including KV fetch duration and kernel-selection time slices

Experiment matrix (runs):
- Var A: baseline (cache cold for long-context requests), 50/100/200 qps, long-context ratio 0.25
- Var B: partial-prefill (30% of long-context tokens primed), same qps sweep
- Var C: full-prefill (100%)
- Var D: partial-prefill + prefetch-worker enabled (early-kv-prefetch=true)
- Each run: 20m steady-state after 5m warmup, repeat 3x per cell

Traffic shape specifics:
- Request payloads: short (30 tokens), medium (180 tokens), long (1200 tokens)
- Long-context requests append earlier conversation fragments (simulated token ids) that trigger more KV lookups
- Priority classes: 80% normal, 20% low-priority (queued behind normal), interleaved arrivals

Key raw numbers (median of 3 runs) — aggregated per-run snapshot:
Throughput (QPS) / p50 / p95 / p99 / notes
100 / 58ms / 120ms / 250ms / baseline
200 / 62ms / 145ms / 410ms / cold fragments more frequent
400 / 85ms / 280ms / 980ms / sustained queuing + KV stalls

Partial-prefill (30%) at 200 qps:
200 / 60ms / 130ms / 300ms / ~27% lower p99 vs baseline at same QPS

Full-prefill at 200 qps:
200 / 58ms / 120ms / 160ms / p99 almost matches p95 baseline, cost to prefill measured ~0.3 tokens/sec per GPU (profiling)

Prefetch-worker enabled (partial case) at 200 qps:
200 / 59ms / 125ms / 210ms / prefetch reduced p99 further by ~30% vs partial without prefetch

Observations / traces:
- p99 outliers correlate with requests that triggered an on-the-fly kernel path switch (quantized->mixed-run) due to cache-miss patterns. Kernel switch accounts for 60–70ms of extra delay in many traces.
- KV fetch latency has bimodal distribution: fast local hits (~2–6ms) vs remote-coalesced fetches (80–160ms). Remote fetches line up with p99 spikes.
- When batching grows (400 qps), increased batch assembly time + tail KV fetches amplify p99 multiplicatively.
- Low-priority requests are often starved during short overloaded bursts; they see higher variance but are good candidates for deferred prefill/backfill strategies.

Hypotheses:
1) Partial prefill + lightweight prefetch worker gives most favorable cost/latency tradeoff vs always full-prefill.
2) Kernel path switch penalty could be reduced by smoothing the decision boundary (e.g., maintain small fallback kernel hot for mixed inputs).
3) Coalescing remote KV fetches and introducing a small async backoff reduces p99 more than naive synchronous retries.

Quick conclusions:
- Full prefill removes the majority of p99 tail but has non-trivial prefill cost; useful for high-value traffic or reserved capacity customers.
- For mixed traffic, a hybrid pattern (30–50% prefill + prefetch worker + async KV coalescing) gives ~25–40% p99 reduction at ~10–15% overhead.
- For bursty ingress, limit batch growth by capping max-batch-wait and prefer more frequent small batches when long-context fraction > 0.2.

Next experiments (actionable):
- Run budgeted-prefill: only prefill high-score conversation fragments (use cheap relevance model to decide). Measure delta in p99 and token-cost.
- Measure kernel warmup: keep fallback kernel resident for short windows (5s) after edge hits; test impact on path-switch penalty.
- Implement remote-KV-coalescer prototype: group remote requests per-shard on 10ms window and benchmark p99 impact.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Attach the specific trace-ids for top 10 p99 offenders from run 2026-02-20_200qps_B (folder on S3).
- Share quick summary with Arjun and Lina + tag JIRA-ENG-7842 for follow-up infra work.
- If validated, propose default partial-prefill policy for Dedicated customers in product meeting (add cost estimate).

End of scratchpad.
summary: Personal scratchpad: measured p99 sensitivity to fragmented KV cache. Partial prefill + prefetch-worker reduces tail significantly vs no prefill; full prefill eliminates most tail but at cost. Next steps: budgeted prefill, kernel warmup, remote-KV coalescer prototyping.
